unit: Pediatric PN daily maintenance convention and fluid allowance calculations

book11.scope: Full printed page 150 / PDF page 158 and its fluid table were previously read as text and rendered images; the table text was rechecked in this unit. The pediatric equation applies only above 20 kg. Adult 30-40 mL/kg/day and other-fluid accounting are distinguished from the pediatric equation.

fda2018.scope: Complete relevant PDF pages 5-6 (dosing considerations) and 8-9 (section 2.8 and Tables 3-6) were read as text and rendered images. All column and row headers, footnotes, age groups, total nutritional requirements, and product-specific dose volumes were reviewed. PDF page 18 reference 1, ASPEN PN Handbook (2014), page 123, was read as text. Four complete pages were rendered and manually viewed. This supports a historical maintenance method, not current 2026 labeling or product availability. Review of the complete 20-page label is not claimed.

fda2021.scope: Complete relevant PDF pages 10-11 (pediatric tables) and 17 (section 8.4) were read as text and rendered images; PDF page 8 dosing text was also read. The later tables omit the older Recommended Nutritional Requirements column. This is not established as the latest label, and removal of that column is not treated as withdrawal of the mathematical convention. No new protein or product dose was adopted. Review of the complete 21-page label is not claimed.

holliday.scope: The original study is reference 31 in ASPEN Nutrition in Clinical Practice (2018), doi:10.1002/ncp.10095. Its complete original publisher abstract, including the formula and water conversion, was exposed in an indexed primary-publisher search result. Direct access redirected to login or traffic validation; the full paper was not accessed or claimed reviewed. This establishes named-method provenance. Complete FDA 2018 tables supply direct numerical support. No historical electrolyte or energy regimen was adopted.

aspenOrder.scope: The prior complete two-page text and rendered review is recorded in pediatric-parenteral-nutrition-compounding-safety-review.json. Both pages were rechecked as text in this unit. Dosing weight, age, nutrition plan, volume, infusion rate, pediatric units, and the distinction between 2-in-1 PN with separate ILE and TNA support checking a stated prescription.

sourceDiscrepancies: Chapter 54 does not contain the lower-weight maintenance formula; Chapter 11 provides only the branch above 20 kg. Lower tiers are supported by the approved FDA 2018 tables rather than inferred from the book.

In FDA 2018 Tables 4-6, the fluid expression in the Recommended Nutritional Requirements column produces a total daily volume despite the row heading mL/kg/day. Do not multiply that completed total by weight again or equate it with a product-specific PN volume.

FDA 2021 tables omit the older nutritional-requirements column and retain product-specific dose volumes. No current product dose, universal fluid target, or withdrawal of the historical convention is inferred. The public 2018 reference is explicitly labeled historical.

The 2018 and 2021 preterm protein tables list 3-4 g/kg/day. These are not substituted for the previously reviewed 2023 ASPEN maximal target of 3.5 g/kg/day. No neonatal fluid protocol or new amino-acid dose is adopted.
The original 1957 full paper was unavailable. Indexed abstract provenance is not a full-paper review; complete relevant FDA 2018 tables provide the numerical evidence.

The questions calculate a stated daily maintenance convention for children aged at least one month. Actual PN volume requires clinical assessment and reconciliation of other fluid sources, product, concentration, access, and rate. No automatic infusion recommendation is added.
